This guide covers advanced programmatic workflows for the `Rwapor` package, including seasonal analysis, multi-year monitoring with DuckDB, and handling mixed-resolution datasets.

## 1. Seasonal Crop Water Productivity Analysis

The `Rwapor` package provides a unified engine, `wapor_run_seasonal_analysis()`, to perform complex seasonal calculations (AETI, ETc, Yield, CWP, Adequacy) in a single step.

### 1.1 Single Season Analysis

This workflow demonstrates how to calculate indicators for a single crop season using a crop mask and local data.

```r
library(Rwapor)

# 1. Define configuration
config <- list(
  period      = c("2023-10-01", "2024-05-31"),
  ref_year    = 1970,           # Historical anchor
  aeti_var    = "L3-AETI-D",
  ret_var     = "L1-RET-D",
  precip_var  = "L1-PCP-D",
  npp_var     = "L3-NPP-D",
  t_var       = "L3-T-D",       # Transpiration support
  data_source = "local",        # Use downloaded files
  folder      = "wapor_data",
  indicators  = c("agg_aeti", "agg_t", "etc", "yield_npp", "adequacy_etc")
)

# 2. Set crop parameters (can be customized)
crop_params <- wapor_crop_defaults("Winter Wheat")

# 3. Run the engine
results <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(
  config      = config,
  crop_params = crop_params,
  rasters     = list(crop_mask = terra::rast("wheat_mask.tif"))
)

# 4. Save the results
wapor_shiny_save_analysis_rasters(results, "output/Winter2023", "Winter2023", config$indicators)
```

### 1.2 Batch Multi-Year Analysis

If you have multiple years of data, you can pass a named list of periods. The engine will automatically loop through them and perform "Smart-Linking" with any season-specific masks.

```r
# Define multiple seasons
periods <- list(
  "Winter2018" = c("2018-10-01", "2019-05-31"),
  "Winter2019" = c("2019-10-01", "2020-05-31"),
  "Winter2020" = c("2020-10-01", "2021-05-31")
)

config$period <- periods

# The engine returns a named list of results for all years
all_results <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(config, crop_params, rasters)

# Save all years at once
wapor_shiny_save_analysis_rasters(all_results, "output/batch_analysis", NULL, config$indicators)
```

### 1.3 Plot-Specific Timing Masks (Heterogeneous Seasons)

For regions where different farm plots have different planting/harvest dates, you can generate custom timing masks from a Vector file and a CSV.

```r
# 1. Generate heterogeneous masks
mask_map <- wapor_vector_to_season_rasters(
  vector_path   = "farm_plots.geojson",
  csv_path      = "planting_dates.csv",
  template_r    = terra::rast("template.tif"),
  id_col        = "plot_id",
  output_folder = "wapor_data/seasonal_masks"
)

# 2. Run analysis
# The engine will automatically detect and apply the correct mask 
# (e.g. Winter2018_start.tif) for each year in your batch.
results <- wapor_run_seasonal_analysis(config, crop_params, rasters)
```

## 2. Continuous Monitoring with DuckDB
...

The monitoring module allows you to maintain a local "Data Cube" that stays synchronized with the WaPOR API.

```r
library(Rwapor)
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)

con <- dbConnect(duckdb::duckdb(), dbdir = "monitoring.duckdb")
pivots <- sf::st_read("pivots.geojson")

# Sync only new data
wapor_run_monitoring(
  con          = con,
  farms_sf     = pivots,
  variables    = c("L3-AETI-D", "L1-RET-D"),
  period       = c("2020-01-01", "2024-04-20"),
  save_rasters = TRUE
)

# Extract a specific blob for custom analysis
blob_data <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT raster_blob FROM farm_rasters LIMIT 1")$raster_blob[[1]]
r <- wapor_raster_from_blob(blob_data)
```

## 3. Handling Mixed Resolutions (L1 vs L3)

When comparing Level 1 (250m) and Level 3 (30m) data, use `terra::resample` to align them.

```r
# Retrieve native blobs
r_aeti_l3 <- wapor_raster_from_blob(blob_aeti) # 30m
r_ret_l1  <- wapor_raster_from_blob(blob_ret)  # 250m

# Resample RET to match AETI grid
r_ret_aligned <- terra::resample(r_ret_l1, r_aeti_l3, method = "bilinear")

# Calculate indicator
r_ratio <- r_aeti_l3 / r_ret_aligned
```

## 4. Enhanced Analysis (Percentile Filtering)

Remove noisy edge pixels by recalculating statistics from saved blobs.

```r
# Recalculate Pivot A1 stats using only the top 95% of pixels
# (Discards the bottom 5% which are often contaminated by dry desert edges)
new_stats <- wapor_recalculate_stats_from_rasters(
  con = con,
  farm_id = "Pivot_A1",
  polygon = pivots[pivots$Name == "Pivot_A1", ],
  threshold_pct = 5
)
```
